tags: why do dogs go crazy after a bath
script: The bath is over, the towel comes out, and suddenly your calm dog turns into a rocket, sprinting through the house and rubbing against every sofa. These after-bath zoomies are so common that almost every dog owner has seen them. One big reason is relief. Many dogs find bath time stressful, so once it's finished, all that built-up tension gets released as pure energy. Another reason is the sensation itself, since wet fur feels heavy and odd, and dogs try to shake and rub it off. Rolling on carpets and furniture also helps dry them faster. Some dogs seem to dislike smelling like shampoo, because their sense of smell is far stronger than ours, so they try to cover that scent with something more familiar, like your couch or bedding. And of course, a bit of excitement from all the attention doesn't hurt either. It's usually harmless fun, so just clear a safe space, keep floors from being slippery, and let them burn it off. To make baths easier, keep them calm, use treats, and finish on something your dog loves.
